author: Ricardo Marques
description: Recipe search, ingredient matching, nutrition filters and a private cookbook for any AI agent.
name: ask.recipes

prompts.name: cook_what_i_have
prompts.title: Cook with what I have
prompts.description: Turn the ingredients on hand into a ranked list of recipes, with what each one is missing.

arguments.name: ingredients

arguments.description: Most time you want to spend, total.

prompts.name: dinner_tonight
prompts.title: Dinner tonight
prompts.description: Pick a well-rated dinner for tonight within a time, serving and diet constraint.

prompts.description: Answer a few questions once about who eats at home, allergies, dislikes, favourites, diets, weeknight time and units, and every search from then on respects them.

tools.name: add_to_pantry
tools.title: Add to the pantry
tools.description: Add or restock pantry items from what the user says in passing: "bought rice and two chickens", "here's what's in the fridge". An item already in the pantry gets the new quantity. Names are matched loosely, so 'Eggs' and 'eggs' are the same item. Returns the whole pantry after the change.

add.description: items to add or update; an item already in the pantry gets the new quantity

quantity.description: optional amount in the user's words, e.g. '6', '500 g', 'half a bag'
optional amount in the user's words, e.g. '6', '500 g', 'half a bag'

tools.name: connect_cookidoo
tools.title: Connect Cookidoo (Thermomix / Bimby)
tools.description: Check whether the user's Cookidoo account (the Thermomix / Bimby recipe platform) is connected, and when it is not, return a one-time link where they enter their Cookidoo login. For "connect my Thermomix", "link my Bimby", or before the first send_to_thermomix. Give the user the link; it works once and expires in 15 minutes.

devices.description: every Thermomix paired with the account

language.description: language of the Cookidoo account; write everything sent to it in this language

machine.description: Thermomix model the recipes are written for

tools.name: cooked_history
tools.title: What the user cooked
tools.description: List what the user cooked and when, newest first, for "what did we cook last week", "when did I last make the lasagna", "what have we been eating". Call it before planning a week so the plan avoids repeating recent dishes and ingredients. Each entry carries the day, the user's note and the recipe summary with its source link. Without since, until or recipe_id it covers the last 30 days.

recipe_id.description: only entries for this recipe, for 'when did I last make the lasagna'; lifts the 30-day default

since.description: first day to include as YYYY-MM-DD; without since, until or recipe_id the last 30 days are returned

until.description: last day to include as YYYY-MM-DD, inclusive

tools.name: create_cookbook
tools.title: Create a cookbook
tools.description: Create an empty cookbook, for "make me a BBQ cookbook". Not needed before save_recipe, which creates a cookbook it does not know. Fails when a cookbook with that name exists already. shared=true makes it a household cookbook, visible to everyone in the user's household.

description.description: one line on what goes in it

shared.description: true to make it a household cookbook that everyone in the user's household sees and saves into, for 'a cookbook for the whole family'; needs a household

tools.name: delete_cookbook
tools.title: Delete a cookbook
tools.description: Delete a cookbook by name. No recipe is lost: any recipe that was only in this cookbook moves to the default cookbook. The default cookbook cannot be deleted.

cookbook.description: name of the cookbook to delete; its recipes are kept and any that were in no other cookbook move to the default one

tools.name: disconnect_cookidoo
tools.title: Disconnect Cookidoo
tools.description: Remove the user's stored Cookidoo login from ask.recipes. Recipes already sent to Cookidoo and recipes imported into ask.recipes stay where they are.

tools.name: find_by_ingredients
tools.title: Find recipes by ingredients on hand
tools.description: Find recipes that use ingredients the user already has: leftovers, a full fridge, an ingredient about to turn. Ranks by how many of those ingredients a recipe uses and how few extra ones it needs. The user's pantry counts as on hand too, so a recipe that only needs pantry staples on top of what was passed ranks as nearly complete; with no ingredients passed it cooks from the pantry alone, for "what can I make with what I have"; when the pantry is empty too, ask_user carries the question to put to the user. Takes the same diet, nutrition and exclude_ingredients filters as search_recipes. Each result links to its source. The user's profile, once saved with update_profile, excludes allergens and dislikes, keeps its diets on and supplies the default time budget; pass max_total_minutes=-1 to lift it. who names the people eating, by name or role, when not everyone is. check, present when the profile has allergens, says to read a recipe's ingredients with get_recipe before recommending it, because a product name can hide an excluded ingredient.

batch_friendly.description: true to leave out dishes cooked per portion, for a crowd; recipes not yet classified stay in

dairy_free.description: only recipes without milk, butter, cheese, cream or yogurt

exclude_ingredients.description: ingredients to leave out for this search, whole-word match on the ingredient list, e.g. ['chicken','brussels sprouts'] to avoid repeating what the week already has; nuts, gluten and dairy as a word apply the matching diet filter; the profile's allergens and dislikes stay excluded on top

feeding.description: how many people are eating, e.g. 10 for a dinner party; from six up, dishes cooked in one vessel (stews, braises, tray bakes, casseroles, soups, roasts) rank ahead of dishes cooked per portion (steaks, burgers, pancakes, stir-fries); nothing is excluded

gluten_free.description: only recipes without wheat, barley, rye, oats or products made from them

ignore_pantry.description: true to match only the ingredients passed and not count the pantry, for 'using just these'

ingredients.description: ingredients to cook with, e.g. ['oats','milk','eggs','skyr','berries']; leave empty to cook from the pantry alone

main_protein.description: only recipes whose main protein is one of these: chicken, turkey, duck, goose, quail, pheasant, guinea_fowl, beef (with veal), pork (with ham, bacon and sausage), lamb (with mutton), goat, venison, bison, rabbit, fish, shrimp (with prawns), seafood (other shellfish, squid, octopus), egg, legume (beans, lentils, chickpeas, tofu), none; e.g. ['beef','pork','lamb'] for red meat or ['fish','shrimp','seafood']; judged from the ingredients, so chicken stock alone does not make a chicken dish

max_calories.description: only recipes with at most this many calories per serving, e.g. 300

max_carbs_g.description: maximum grams of carbohydrates per serving

max_fat_g.description: maximum grams of fat per serving

max_sugar_g.description: maximum grams of sugar per serving

min_calories.description: only recipes with at least this many calories per serving

min_fiber_g.description: minimum grams of fiber per serving

min_protein_g.description: minimum grams of protein per serving, e.g. 10

min_rating.description: only recipes rated at least this many stars, source ratings and ask.recipes stars averaged together; recipes nobody has rated yet and private uploads stay in; off unless passed

min_reviews.description: only recipes with at least this many ratings, source and ask.recipes together; recipes with no rating at all and private uploads stay in; off unless passed

nut_free.description: only recipes without tree nuts or peanuts; coconut counts as nut-free

query.description: optional free-text to narrow results, e.g. 'breakfast pancakes'

vegan.description: only vegan recipes: vegetarian and no eggs, dairy or honey

vegetarian.description: only vegetarian recipes: no meat, poultry, fish, seafood or gelatin in the ingredients

who.description: who is eating, by the names or roles saved as people on the profile, e.g. ['Dad','Ana'] or ['adults'] when the kids are out, ['kids'] when only they eat; only those people's allergens and dislikes apply on top of the household's; leave empty for everyone

annotations.title: Find recipes by ingredients on hand

tools.name: get_household
tools.title: Who shares the kitchen
tools.description: Read the user's household: its name and who is in it, by the names they go by at home. Members share one pantry, one cooking diary and any cookbook marked shared, and each member's own allergens and dislikes apply when anyone in the household searches for everyone. in_household=false means the user shares a kitchen with nobody yet; invite_to_household starts one. For "who's in my household", "is my partner connected".

in_household.description: false when this account shares a kitchen with nobody yet

creator.description: the member who created the household; the only one who can remove others

tools.name: get_pantry
tools.title: What is in the pantry
tools.description: List what the user has told you is in their kitchen: pantry, fridge and freezer, with quantities when they gave one. For "what do I have", before suggesting a shopping list, or to check an ingredient before recommending a recipe. find_by_ingredients with no ingredients searches from this list directly.

quantity.description: optional amount in the user's words, e.g. '6', '500 g', 'half a bag'

tools.name: get_profile
tools.title: How the household eats
tools.description: Read what is saved about how the user eats: how many are eating, allergens, dislikes, likes, diets, cuisines, the usual weeknight time budget, units, daily calorie or macro goals, and the people in the household, each with a role such as kid or adult and what applies to them alone. Household allergens and dislikes are excluded from every search; a person's apply whenever they are eating, which is everyone unless a search passes who. Diets stay on and the time budget is the default time limit, so you rarely need to pass them yourself; read likes and cuisines to steer suggestions. Call it before planning a week and when the user asks what you know about them. set=false means nothing is saved yet: offer the set_up_my_kitchen questions once.

household.description: present when the user shares a kitchen with other ask.recipes accounts; their allergens and dislikes apply to searches for everyone

in_household.description: false when this account shares a kitchen with nobody yet

creator.description: the member who created the household; the only one who can remove others

set.description: false when nothing has been saved yet

tools.name: get_recipe
tools.title: Get a recipe in full
tools.description: Get one recipe in full: ingredients, step-by-step instructions, times, yield, nutrition, rating (source ratings and ask.recipes stars averaged, with the user's own as my_rating) and its source link. For when the user picks a recipe from a search or asks how to make it. Pass servings to scale the ingredient quantities, e.g. for meal prep or a crowd; nutrition_for says whether the nutrition numbers are per serving or for the whole yield. Amounts come back in the units saved on the profile: metric turns cups and ounces into grams and millilitres (dry goods by weight, liquids by volume, spoons stay spoons) and oven temperatures and pan sizes in the steps into Celsius and centimetres; us does the reverse; units in the result says which applied, empty means as the source wrote it. Pass units to override for one call.

id.description: recipe id from a previous search

servings.description: scale ingredient quantities to this many servings; when the recipe's yield does not state servings the recipe comes back unscaled with scale_note saying so, nutrition stays per serving

units.description: metric or us; converts the ingredient amounts and the temperatures and pan sizes in the steps; defaults to the units saved on the profile, leave empty unless the user asks for the other system this once

tools.name: import_cookidoo_recipe
tools.title: Import a Cookidoo recipe
tools.description: Copy one Cookidoo recipe into the user's private ask.recipes collection, so the agent can read it in full, adapt it, build a shopping list, or compare it with other recipes. Imported recipes are visible only to this user and cannot be shared. Importing the same recipe again refreshes the copy.

cookidoo_id.description: Cookidoo recipe id such as r123456 or a created-recipe id, from search_cookidoo, list_cookidoo_recipes or the recipe's Cookidoo URL

tools.name: import_recipes
tools.title: Import a recipe app export
tools.description: Return a one-time link where the user drops the export file from their recipe app: Paprika (.paprikarecipes), Mela (.melarecipes), Crouton (.crumb) or a zip of recipe pages carrying schema.org Recipe markup. Every recipe becomes a private recipe visible only to this user, in a cookbook named after the file, with its photo; Paprika star ratings become my_rating, nutrition is estimated afterwards. For "import my Paprika recipes", "bring my recipe collection over", or whenever the user has more than a few recipes to add at once; upload_recipe stays the tool for a single recipe. Give the user the link as is; it works once and expires in an hour. Files up to 100 MB and 3000 recipes; bigger libraries go in by category, duplicates are skipped on a second upload. Then suggest list_saved with the new cookbook once they say it is done.

how_to_export.description: where the export lives in each app

import_url.description: one-time page where the user drops the export file; works once, expires in an hour

tools.name: invite_to_household
tools.title: Invite someone to the household
tools.description: Create a one-time link that lets another ask.recipes user join the user's household, for "add my wife to my household", "share my pantry with Sam", "connect my partner's account". The first call creates the household, so pass my_name (what the family calls the user) and optionally household_name. The person opens the link, enters their name and email, confirms a 6-digit code and is in; an account is created for them when they have none. On joining, their pantry merges into the shared one and their cooking diary becomes the household's. Give the user the link as is to forward; it works once and expires in a day. Up to 6 members, and an account can be in one household at a time.

household_name.description: a name for the household when creating it, e.g. 'Casa Silva' or 'Home'; defaults to Home

my_name.description: what the household calls the user, e.g. 'Dad' or 'Ana'; required the first time, when the household is created, and shown to the person invited

in_household.description: false when this account shares a kitchen with nobody yet

creator.description: the member who created the household; the only one who can remove others

join_url.description: one-time link the user sends to the person joining; works once and expires in a day

tools.name: leave_household
tools.title: Leave the household
tools.description: Take the user out of their household, for "leave the household", "stop sharing my kitchen". The shared pantry, diary entries and shared cookbooks stay with the household; the user starts again with an empty pantry and keeps their own diary entries. When the last member leaves, the household is gone. Confirm with the user before calling.

left.description: name of the household the user left

tools.name: list_cookbooks
tools.title: List cookbooks
tools.description: List the user's cookbooks with how many recipes each holds, for "what cookbooks do I have", or before saving when the user says "the usual one". Every user has a default cookbook; the others are named by the user, e.g. Stews, BBQ, Christmas. Cookbooks shared with the household carry shared=true and appear for every member.

tools.name: list_cookidoo_recipes
tools.title: List the user's own Cookidoo recipes
tools.description: List the recipes the user created on Cookidoo, including ones sent there by send_to_thermomix, for "what is on my Bimby", "my Thermomix recipes", "read recipes from my Cookidoo". This is the Bimby side; list_saved is the ask.recipes side. Returns Cookidoo ids to pass to import_cookidoo_recipe. Names and links only until the user imports one.

annotations.title: List the user's own Cookidoo recipes

tools.name: list_saved
tools.title: List saved recipes
tools.description: List the recipes the user saved in ask.recipes, for "my recipes", "what did I save", "what's in my Stews cookbook". Each recipe lists the cookbooks it is in and the user's note; pass cookbook to see one cookbook only. Each also carries when it was last cooked and how many times, when mark_cooked recorded it. Not the Thermomix / Bimby / Cookidoo side; that is list_cookidoo_recipes.

cookbook.description: only recipes in this cookbook, by name; leave empty for every saved recipe, each listed with the cookbooks it is in

tools.name: mark_cooked
tools.title: Mark a recipe as cooked
tools.description: Record that the user cooked a recipe, for "we made that tonight", "cooked the curry yesterday", "the lasagna was a hit". One entry per time it was cooked, with the day and an optional note on how it went. Pass date when the user names a day other than today. The recipe need not be saved. Pass rating when the user gave a verdict in stars or words, so the cook and the rating land in one call. Returns the entry plus how many times and when this recipe was last cooked.

date.description: the day it was cooked as YYYY-MM-DD in the user's calendar, e.g. yesterday's date for 'we made it last night'; empty means today

note.description: what the user said about how it went, e.g. 'kids loved it, double the sauce next time'; at most 200 characters

rating.description: the user's stars for the recipe, 1 to 5, when they gave a verdict: 'it was a hit' is 5, 'fine' is 3, 'never again' is 1; replaces their earlier rating of this recipe; leave out when they said nothing about how it was

tools.name: rate_recipe
tools.title: Rate a recipe
tools.description: Record the user's stars for a recipe, 1 to 5, for "five stars", "that one was a 3", "best curry we've had", with an optional note on why. One rating per user and recipe; rating again replaces it. The stars join the recipe's rating: the rating and rating_count every tool returns average the source site's ratings and ask.recipes users' stars together, and the user's own stars come back as my_rating. When the user also says they cooked it, mark_cooked with rating does both in one call.

note.description: why, in the user's words, e.g. 'too sweet, halve the sugar'; at most 200 characters; empty keeps the note from the earlier rating

stars.description: 1 to 5 stars; replaces the user's earlier rating of this recipe

tools.name: remove_from_household
tools.title: Remove someone from the household
tools.description: Take another member out of the user's household by the name get_household lists, for "remove Sam from the household". Only the household's creator can do it; when the creator leaves, the longest-standing member takes over. The removed person keeps their account and their own diary entries; the shared pantry and cookbooks stay. Confirm with the user before calling.

name.description: the member's name as get_household lists it

in_household.description: false when this account shares a kitchen with nobody yet

creator.description: the member who created the household; the only one who can remove others

tools.name: remove_from_pantry
tools.title: Remove from the pantry
tools.description: Take items out of the pantry for "used the last onions", "we're out of milk", or empty it with all=true when the user lists what is in the kitchen now, then add_to_pantry. Names are matched loosely. Returns the whole pantry after the change.

all.description: true to empty the pantry, for 'here is what's in my kitchen now' before add_to_pantry

remove.description: item names to take out, for 'used the last onions', 'we're out of milk'

quantity.description: optional amount in the user's words, e.g. '6', '500 g', 'half a bag'

tools.name: save_recipe
tools.title: Save a recipe
tools.description: Save a recipe to one of the user's cookbooks, for "save that one", "keep this", "put it in my BBQ cookbook". Pass cookbook when the user names one; it is created on first use. Without one the recipe goes to the default cookbook. A recipe can sit in several cookbooks; saving it again to the same one only updates the note.

cookbook.description: cookbook to save into, by name, e.g. 'Stews' or 'Christmas'; created when it does not exist yet; leave empty for the default cookbook

note.description: the user's own note on this recipe in this cookbook, e.g. 'half the chilli, kids loved it'

tools.name: search_cookidoo
tools.title: Search the user's Cookidoo
tools.description: Search Cookidoo's catalogue of Thermomix recipes through the user's connected account, for "find a Bimby recipe for", "what does Cookidoo have for", "search my Bimby for". For the user's own recipes use list_cookidoo_recipes. Returns Cookidoo ids to pass to import_cookidoo_recipe. Cookidoo recipes are the user's subscription content: never quote them beyond name and link unless the user imports them.

query.description: dish or ingredients to look for in Cookidoo's own recipes, in the user's Cookidoo language

tools.name: search_recipes
tools.title: Search recipes
tools.description: Search recipes for a what-to-cook or what-to-eat question: dinner tonight, cooking for guests, a quick weeknight meal, a protein or calorie target, macros for a cut or a bulk, meal prep for the week. Every result links to its source. rating and rating_count average the source site's ratings with ask.recipes users' stars; my_rating is the user's own. Filters by time, rating, review count, diet (vegetarian, vegan, gluten_free, dairy_free, nut_free, judged from the ingredient list) and nutrition (calories, protein, fat, carbs, sugar, fiber per serving as reported by the source). A nutrition filter only returns recipes whose yield is stated in servings, so the numbers are per serving; recipes without nutrition data are excluded. Results rank by how closely they match the query; min_rating and min_reviews cut rated recipes below a threshold only when passed, and never drop a recipe nobody has rated or a private upload. exclude_ingredients leaves out recipes using any of the ingredients named, for building a week without repeats. main_protein keeps recipes whose main protein is one of the values passed, for week rules like one chicken, two fish and three vegetarian dinners; every result carries main_protein. The user's profile, once saved with update_profile, applies on top: allergens and dislikes are always excluded, its diets are always on, and its time budget is the default when max_total_minutes is not passed; pass max_total_minutes=-1 to lift it. When people are saved on the profile, who names those eating tonight, by name or by role such as adults or kids, and only their allergens and dislikes apply, for "the kids aren't home"; empty means everyone. ask_user, when present, says no profile is saved yet and what to offer. check, present when the profile has allergens, reminds you that exclusions match whole words and a sauce or spice mix can hide one; read the ingredients with get_recipe before recommending.

batch_friendly.description: true to leave out dishes cooked per portion, for a crowd; recipes not yet classified stay in

dairy_free.description: only recipes without milk, butter, cheese, cream or yogurt

exclude_ingredients.description: ingredients to leave out for this search, whole-word match on the ingredient list, e.g. ['chicken','brussels sprouts'] to avoid repeating what the week already has; nuts, gluten and dairy as a word apply the matching diet filter; the profile's allergens and dislikes stay excluded on top

feeding.description: how many people are eating, e.g. 10 for a dinner party; from six up, dishes cooked in one vessel (stews, braises, tray bakes, casseroles, soups, roasts) rank ahead of dishes cooked per portion (steaks, burgers, pancakes, stir-fries); nothing is excluded

gluten_free.description: only recipes without wheat, barley, rye, oats or products made from them

main_protein.description: only recipes whose main protein is one of these: chicken, turkey, duck, goose, quail, pheasant, guinea_fowl, beef (with veal), pork (with ham, bacon and sausage), lamb (with mutton), goat, venison, bison, rabbit, fish, shrimp (with prawns), seafood (other shellfish, squid, octopus), egg, legume (beans, lentils, chickpeas, tofu), none; e.g. ['beef','pork','lamb'] for red meat or ['fish','shrimp','seafood']; judged from the ingredients, so chicken stock alone does not make a chicken dish

max_calories.description: only recipes with at most this many calories per serving, e.g. 300

max_carbs_g.description: maximum grams of carbohydrates per serving

max_fat_g.description: maximum grams of fat per serving

max_sugar_g.description: maximum grams of sugar per serving

max_total_minutes.description: only recipes taking at most this many minutes total

min_calories.description: only recipes with at least this many calories per serving

min_fiber_g.description: minimum grams of fiber per serving

min_protein_g.description: minimum grams of protein per serving, e.g. 10

min_rating.description: only recipes rated at least this many stars, e.g. 4.5, source ratings and ask.recipes stars averaged together; recipes nobody has rated yet and private uploads stay in; off unless passed

min_reviews.description: only recipes with at least this many ratings, source and ask.recipes together, e.g. 25; recipes with no rating at all and private uploads stay in; off unless passed

nut_free.description: only recipes without tree nuts or peanuts; coconut counts as nut-free

vegan.description: only vegan recipes: vegetarian and no eggs, dairy or honey

tools.name: send_to_thermomix
tools.title: Send a recipe to the Thermomix
tools.description: Send one recipe to the user's Cookidoo account as a private created recipe, so it shows on their Thermomix / Bimby with guided cooking. For "send this to my Thermomix", "put it on my Bimby", "cook this on the TM6". First get_recipe, then rewrite the recipe for the Cookidoo account: name, ingredients and steps in the account's language (connect_cookidoo returns it), amounts in grams and millilitres since the Thermomix weighs everything, steps as Thermomix steps with time, temperature, speed, direction or mode. Pass name, ingredients and steps; show the user the rewritten steps before sending. Each call creates a new Cookidoo recipe. Thermomix step settings, for rewriting a recipe before send_to_thermomix: each step is one action with at most one setting block. Times are seconds. Chop: 5-10 s / speed 5-7. Sauté onion and garlic: 3-5 min / 120 °C / speed 1. Simmer sauces and soups: 15-25 min / 100 °C / speed 1, with direction CCW when pieces must stay whole. Blend soup: 1 min / speed 10. Whip cream: speed 3.5 with the butterfly, write that in the text. Melt chocolate: 50 °C / speed 2. Knead bread: mode dough for 2-3 min. Steam: mode steaming, or varoma temperature with the Varoma dish. Rice: mode rice_cooker. Modes depend on the model connect_cookidoo reports: a TM31 has none, a TM5 only dough and turbo, TM6 and TM7 all of them; on an older model write the step with time, temperature and speed instead, and the server refuses a mode the machine lacks. Keep the ingredient amounts in the step text so the screen shows them. Steps without settings are fine for prep done outside the machine.

hints.description: optional tips shown under the recipe on Cookidoo

id.description: recipe id from a search, get_recipe, list_saved or upload

ingredients.description: one ingredient per entry in the account's language with metric amounts in g or ml, e.g. '200 g cebola, em pedaços'; the stored list is sent verbatim when omitted

machine.description: TM31, TM5, TM6 or TM7, only when the user names a paired machine other than the connected one

name.description: recipe name in the Cookidoo account's language; the stored name is used when omitted

steps.description: the recipe rewritten as Thermomix steps with settings, in the account's language; when omitted the recipe's plain steps are sent without settings

direction.description: CCW for reverse blade (keeps pieces whole: stews, rice, fish); omit for normal

mode.description: guided mode instead of manual settings: dough, browning, turbo, steaming, blend, warm_up, rice_cooker

speed.description: one of soft 0.5 1 1.5 2 2.5 3 3.5 4 4.5 5 5.5 6 6.5 7 7.5 8 8.5 9 9.5 10; soft is the gentle stirring speed

text.description: the step as the cook reads it on the Thermomix screen; one action per step. Settings are appended as a Cookidoo label such as 5 min/100°C/vel 1, so leave them out of the text

time_seconds.description: run time in seconds for this step, e.g. 300 for 5 min

annotations.title: Send a recipe to the Thermomix

tools.name: share_recipe
tools.title: Create a share link
tools.description: Create a share link for a recipe, for "send this to my wife", "share it with Tom", "give me a link", "add this to MacroFactor". Works for any recipe the user can read: the corpus, their own uploads and the uploads of people in their household. Returns a share.ask.recipes URL that opens without an account and is not listed or indexed; the page credits the recipe's source and its licence and carries schema.org Recipe markup, so apps that import a recipe from a link can read it. Recipes imported from Cookidoo cannot be shared.

id.description: id of a recipe the user uploaded

tools.name: unsave_recipe
tools.title: Remove a saved recipe
tools.description: Take a recipe out of the user's cookbooks, for "remove that from my saved", "take it out of Christmas". With cookbook set it leaves only that cookbook; without it the recipe is removed from every cookbook. The recipe itself stays searchable.

cookbook.description: take it out of this cookbook only; leave empty to remove it from every cookbook

tools.name: update_cookbook
tools.title: Rename or describe a cookbook
tools.description: Rename a cookbook, change its description, or share it with the household, for "call it Sunday Roasts instead" or "share my Christmas cookbook with the family". Recipes stay where they are. The default cookbook stays personal.

cookbook.description: current name of the cookbook to change

description.description: new description; leave empty to keep it

name.description: new name; leave empty to keep it

shared.description: true moves the cookbook to the household so every member sees it, false makes it personal to this user again; leave out to keep it as is

tools.name: update_household
tools.title: Rename the household or the user in it
tools.description: Rename the household or change what it calls the user, for "call our household Casa Silva", "in the household I'm Mum, not Ana". Names are what who on a search and cooked_by in the diary use.

household_name.description: new name for the household; leave empty to keep it

my_name.description: new name for the user inside the household; leave empty to keep it

in_household.description: false when this account shares a kitchen with nobody yet

creator.description: the member who created the household; the only one who can remove others

annotations.title: Rename the household or the user in it

tools.name: update_profile
tools.title: Remember how the household eats
tools.description: Save what the user says about how they eat so it holds across sessions and clients: "we don't eat cilantro" is add_dislikes, "my daughter can't have berries or tomatoes" is add_allergens, "we love meat" is add_likes, "weeknights are 30 minutes max" is time_budget_minutes, "we're five" is household_size, "grams please" is units=metric. Only the fields passed change; lists are added to or removed from, never replaced, so nothing already saved is lost. Pass 0 for a number to clear it. Something one person cannot or will not eat goes on that person under people, so a search with who can leave it out when they are not at the table; what everyone avoids goes on the household lists. Give each person a role (kid, adult, parent, guest) when the user says it, so who can name a group. From then on allergens and dislikes are excluded from every search as whole words, vegetarian, vegan, gluten_free, dairy_free and nut_free diets stay on, and the time budget is the default time limit. Returns the whole profile after the change; read it back to the user in one short list. When allergens were added it carries a note to pass on once: exclusions match whole words, so for a serious allergy the user should still read ingredients and labels themselves.

add_allergens.description: ingredients nobody in the household may eat, medical or otherwise, one per entry, e.g. ['peanuts','berries','tomatoes']; excluded from every search as whole words

add_cuisines.description: cuisines the household likes, e.g. ['italian','mexican','thai']; stored for you to read

add_diets.description: diets followed; vegetarian, vegan, gluten_free, dairy_free and nut_free switch the matching filter on for every search, any other value is stored for you to read

add_dislikes.description: ingredients the household avoids by taste, e.g. ['cilantro','mushrooms']; excluded from every search as whole words

add_likes.description: ingredients or dishes the household loves, e.g. ['meat','pasta','spicy food']; nothing is filtered on them, read them to steer what you suggest

calories_per_day.description: daily calorie goal when the user tracks one; 0 clears it

carbs_g_per_day.description: daily carbohydrate goal in grams; 0 clears it

fat_g_per_day.description: daily fat goal in grams; 0 clears it

household_size.description: how many people usually eat, e.g. 5 for two adults and three children; 0 clears it

people.description: people in the household with a role and what applies to them alone: 'Sam, our kid, can't have berries' is people=[{name:'Sam', role:'kid', add_allergens:['berries']}]; what everyone avoids goes on the household lists instead. Each entry changes only that person and only the fields passed

add_allergens.description: ingredients this person cannot eat; excluded whenever they are eating

add_dislikes.description: ingredients this person avoids by taste; excluded whenever they are eating

add_likes.description: what this person loves; read, never filtered

name.description: the person's name as the user says it, e.g. 'Sam' or 'Dad'; matched case-insensitively, created on first use

role.description: one word for who they are in the household, e.g. 'kid', 'adult', 'parent', 'guest'; who on a search accepts a role as well as a name, so 'the kids are out' is who=['adults']; empty string clears it

protein_g_per_day.description: daily protein goal in grams; 0 clears it

remove_people.description: names to take off the profile

time_budget_minutes.description: most minutes a usual dinner may take in total; becomes the default time limit on every search; 0 clears it

units.description: metric or us, the measurements the user wants to read; get_recipe converts amounts and oven temperatures to it; empty string clears it

household.description: present when the user shares a kitchen with other ask.recipes accounts; their allergens and dislikes apply to searches for everyone

in_household.description: false when this account shares a kitchen with nobody yet

creator.description: the member who created the household; the only one who can remove others

set.description: false when nothing has been saved yet

tools.name: upload_recipe
tools.title: Upload a private recipe
tools.description: Add a recipe the user supplies themselves: pasted in, dictated, a family recipe they want kept, or a web page they point at. For a web page, pass the page's raw HTML or its JSON-LD as markup together with source_url; the server extracts the facts. Each call creates a new private recipe, visible only to this user in searches and saves.

ingredients.description: one ingredient per entry, with quantities, e.g. '2 cups rolled oats'

markup.description: for a recipe from a web page: the page's raw HTML, or just its schema.org/Recipe JSON-LD block, as fetched by the agent; the server extracts name, ingredients, steps, times, nutrition and rating from it, so the other fields can stay empty

name.description: recipe name; may be left empty when markup carries the recipe

source_url.description: the web page the recipe came from, if any; kept as attribution on the private copy
